supportTiers.label: Immediate validation and support candidate
supportTiers.fullLabel: Tier 1: Immediate validation / intensive support candidate
supportTiers.meaning: Top 10% support need. These schools are candidates for manual validation and early support.
supportTiers.risk: Low publication visibility or weak capacity signals may hide specific support needs.
supportTiers.support: Use follow-up validation, basic planning support, teacher development, governance checks, infrastructure review, and contextual support where needed.

supportTiers.label: Targeted capacity-building candidate
supportTiers.meaning: Next 15% support need. These schools may need targeted help before AI funding becomes classroom practice.
supportTiers.risk: Foundational capacity may be too thin for rapid implementation without support.
supportTiers.support: Provide capacity-building packages, planning templates, teacher release time, and procurement or governance guidance.

supportTiers.label: General monitoring and standard support
supportTiers.meaning: Middle 50% support need. These schools can receive standard support while monitoring visible implementation progress.
supportTiers.risk: Implementation may still be uneven across teachers, subjects, and documentation practices.
supportTiers.support: Use standard grant guidance, common teacher resources, light-touch monitoring, and optional implementation clinics.

supportTiers.label: Lower immediate support need / peer-learning candidate
supportTiers.fullLabel: Tier 4: Lower immediate support need / peer-learning candidate
supportTiers.meaning: Lowest 25% support need. These schools show stronger visible capacity or lower immediate support need.
supportTiers.risk: Do not convert stronger visible evidence into a prestige ranking.
supportTiers.support: Invite voluntary peer learning, resource exchange, demonstration lessons, and mentoring without treating this as a league table.
